meta.label: Electricity suppliers
tradeoffLabels: lowest bill, protected by the price cap
meta.attribution: Covers domestic electricity suppliers in Great Britain, meaning England, Scotland and Wales. Northern Ireland has separate energy regulation and is not included here. Renewable share and fuel mix figures come from each supplier's own Ofgem-mandated Fuel Mix Disclosure, published every October, or from Citizens Advice's compiled fuel mix data where a supplier's own disclosure page could not be read directly. Customer service scores come from the Citizens Advice Energy Supplier Star Rating for April to June 2026, which covers suppliers with more than 25,000 customer accounts and is compiled by Citizens Advice as the statutory consumer advocate for energy, not by a switching site. A tariff marketed as '100 per cent renewable' is usually backed by Renewable Energy Guarantees of Origin (REGO) certificates bought separately from the electricity itself, which on their own do not prove the supplier funded new renewable generation. Ofgem has recognized only three suppliers, Ecotricity, Good Energy and 100Green (formerly Green Energy UK), as giving renewable generation support beyond what subsidies and obligations already require, and has exempted their tariffs from the price cap on that basis. Every other supplier's renewable tariff here relies on REGO certificates unless its own page says otherwise. Prices change every three months with the Ofgem price cap and vary by region and payment method; check a supplier's current Tariff Information Label before switching. Community energy schemes and home solar generation are separate decisions in this catalogue. Suggest changes via Contribute.

products.name: British Gas
products.description: The largest domestic electricity and gas supplier in Great Britain, owned by Centrica. Its standard tariffs sit at the regulated price cap, and its dedicated renewable product is backed by REGO certificates rather than new generation.

price.note: British Gas's standard variable and default electricity tariffs cannot charge more than the level Ofgem sets and updates every three months under the energy price cap.

environment.note: British Gas's fuel mix for 1 April 2025 to 31 March 2026 was 45 per cent renewable, 46 per cent nuclear, 7 per cent gas, 1 per cent coal and 1 per cent other, giving 91 per cent zero carbon electricity against a UK average of 62 per cent.

transparency.note: British Gas's own energy sources page explains that suppliers back renewable tariffs with Renewable Energy Guarantees of Origin certificates rather than delivering specific green electrons to a customer's home.

accessibility.note: Citizens Advice gave British Gas an overall star rating of 2.61 out of 5 for April to June 2026, ranking 14th of 16 suppliers, with a complaints score of 1.0 out of 5 from 68.8 complaints per 10,000 customers, its weakest category.

products.name: EDF Energy
products.description: A large supplier whose electricity is mostly nuclear rather than renewable. It markets zero carbon and renewable products, but its public fuel mix page does not mention REGO certificates.

price.note: EDF's default electricity tariff is bound by the same Ofgem price cap as every supplier without a derogation.

environment.note: EDF's fuel mix for April 2024 to March 2025 was 54.8 per cent nuclear, 21.0 per cent gas, 18.2 per cent renewables, 4.2 per cent coal and 1.8 per cent other.

transparency.note: EDF's fuel mix page names which tariffs are sold as zero carbon or renewable and says the electricity it buys for them 'is supplied into the National Grid' and that customers receive it through the grid, 'not directly from zero-carbon generators.' Unlike British Gas's equivalent page, it does not mention REGO certificates.

accessibility.note: Citizens Advice gave EDF Energy an overall star rating of 2.96 out of 5 for April to June 2026, ranking 10th of 16 suppliers.

products.name: Octopus Energy
products.description: A fast-growing independent supplier reporting 86.4 per cent renewables in its April 2024 to March 2025 fuel mix, with billions of pounds committed to wind, solar and battery projects it owns or has long-term contracts with.

price.note: Octopus Energy's headline tariffs are bound by the Ofgem price cap in the same way as other suppliers without a derogation.

environment.note: Octopus reports a fuel mix of 86.4 per cent renewables and 13.6 per cent nuclear for 1 April 2024 to 31 March 2025, and says its generation arm manages about 4GW of renewable electricity across 240 projects with a combined asset value of 6 billion pounds, and that it committed a further 15 billion pounds in July 2023 to offshore wind for 12GW of capacity.

transparency.note: Octopus's green page explains that renewable and other generators all feed the same National Grid, and that it matches customer usage to renewable generation through Power Purchase Agreements with more than 700 UK generators rather than delivering separate electrons to each home.

accessibility.note: Citizens Advice gave Octopus Energy an overall star rating of 3.67 out of 5 for April to June 2026, ranking 5th of 16 suppliers.

products.name: OVO Energy
products.description: OVO stopped buying standard renewable certificates in 2023, so its headline fuel mix disclosure looks low. Its Greener Electricity option buys power directly from renewable generators, for an added fee.

price.note: OVO's Greener Electricity page prices the upgrade to 100% renewable electricity at 8 pounds a month, for Direct Debit customers, added to the monthly bill, and says 40 pounds a year of it goes to supporting new independent UK generators. The page does not describe the standard tariff price.

environment.note: OVO says it stopped using REGO certificates as standard in 2023, so its fuel mix for April 2025 to March 2026 is 12 per cent renewables, 64 per cent natural gas, 12 per cent coal, 7 per cent nuclear and 5 per cent other, and it says that 'on average, 48% of the power flowing into homes came from greener sources.' It also says it buys electricity for its Greener Electricity customers directly from renewable generators and invests in new, independent renewable power.

transparency.note: OVO's own fuel mix page says 'REGOs don’t actually make the UK electricity grid any greener' and that green tariffs 'alone don’t generate any more green energy or give you 100% green energy at home.'

accessibility.note: Citizens Advice gave OVO Energy an overall star rating of 3.65 out of 5 for April to June 2026, ranking 6th of 16 suppliers.

products.name: E.ON Next
products.description: E.ON Next's renewable tariff, Next Gust, is backed by agreements with UK wind generators, though the company is clear that the electricity itself still comes from the shared National Grid.

price.note: E.ON Next's default electricity tariff sits under the Ofgem price cap along with other suppliers that hold no derogation.

environment.note: E.ON Next's fuel mix for 1 April 2024 to 31 March 2025 was 31.3 per cent renewable, 51.5 per cent gas, 10.2 per cent coal, 2.7 per cent nuclear and 4.3 per cent other, against a UK average of 42.1 per cent renewable for the same period.

transparency.note: E.ON's news release of 2 June 2026 on the relaunched Next Gust tariff says it gives '100% renewable electricity, backed by agreements with UK wind generators' and states plainly that 'The electricity supplied to your home comes from the National Grid.'

accessibility.note: Citizens Advice gave E.ON Next an overall star rating of 3.71 out of 5 for April to June 2026, ranking 3rd of 16 suppliers.

products.name: ScottishPower
products.description: One of the long-established Big Six suppliers, owned by Iberdrola. Its published fuel mix shows one of the lowest renewable shares among the suppliers in this list.

price.note: ScottishPower's default tariff is bound by the same Ofgem price cap as other suppliers without a derogation.

environment.note: Citizens Advice's April to June 2026 supplier page records ScottishPower's fuel mix as 84 per cent fossil fuel, 7 per cent renewable, 4 per cent nuclear and 5 per cent other. The page does not state the period the fuel mix covers.

accessibility.note: Citizens Advice gave ScottishPower an overall star rating of 2.76 out of 5 for April to June 2026, ranking 12th of 16 suppliers, with 76.4 complaints per 10,000 customers.

products.name: Good Energy
products.description: A small independent supplier that buys power directly from more than 3,300 British renewable generators. Ofgem has recognized its tariffs as delivering renewable support beyond subsidies, and its standard tariff is exempt from the price cap.

price.note: Ofgem has granted Good Energy an enduring exemption from the default tariff cap for its renewable Standard Variable Tariffs, and states explicitly that it has not assessed whether the exempted tariffs are good value for consumers.

environment.note: Good Energy says all its tariffs are matched with 100 per cent renewable electricity bought directly from over 3,300 British generators, and that it achieved a real time match between generation and demand 87 per cent of the time, for the fuel mix disclosure period April 2025 to March 2026.

transparency.note: Good Energy publishes its real time matching percentage and the breakdown of its fuel mix by technology, 55 per cent wind, 27 per cent biogeneration, 9 per cent hydro and 9 per cent solar for April 2025 to March 2026, rather than a single headline renewable figure.

accessibility.note: Citizens Advice gave Good Energy an overall star rating of 3.68 out of 5 for April to June 2026, ranking 4th of 16 suppliers.

products.name: Ecotricity
products.description: Founded in 1995 to sell green electricity as a mainstream product, Ecotricity has built its own wind and solar parks over three decades rather than only buying certificates. Its renewable tariffs are also exempt from the Ofgem price cap.

price.note: Ofgem has granted The Renewable Energy Company Limited, trading as Ecotricity, an enduring exemption from the default tariff cap for its renewable Standard Variable Tariffs, and states it has not assessed whether the exempted tariffs are good value for consumers.

environment.note: Ecotricity's June 2025 news article says that over the past 30 years it has built 24 wind parks, three sun parks and one green gasmill, 'all with the money from our customers’ bills,' and reports 180GWh of its own generation in each of 2023 and 2024. The article does not give the share of customer supply met by its own generation.

transparency.note: Ecotricity's fuel mix page shows 100 per cent renewables for 2024/25 against a 42.1 per cent UK average, and says its 'domestic and business customers receive electricity via the National Grid and Distribution Network and not directly from our green energy generators.' The page does not break down what share of customer supply comes from Ecotricity's own generation against electricity it buys in.

accessibility.note: Citizens Advice gave Ecotricity an overall star rating of 3.40 out of 5 for April to June 2026, ranking 8th of 16 suppliers.

links.label: How much green energy Ecotricity generates

products.name: 100Green
products.description: Formerly Green Energy UK, 100Green buys electricity through Power Purchase Agreements with independent generators and holds a REGO certificate for every unit it supplies, audited annually by Ofgem. It is one of three suppliers Ofgem has exempted from the price cap for genuine additionality.

price.note: Ofgem has granted Green Energy UK Plc, now trading as 100Green, an enduring exemption from the default tariff cap for its renewable Standard Variable Tariffs, and states it has not assessed whether the exempted tariffs are good value for consumers.

environment.note: 100Green's own energy page shows a 100 per cent renewable electricity fuel mix for 1 April 2024 to 31 March 2025 against 42.1 per cent renewables for the UK, and says its renewable energy is transmitted through the national grid and distributed to homes like any other.

transparency.note: 100Green's FAQ explains in plain terms what a Power Purchase Agreement and a REGO certificate are, states it holds a REGO for every megawatt hour it supplies, and says the certification process is audited annually by Ofgem.

accessibility.note: Citizens Advice gave 100Green an overall star rating of 3.90 out of 5 for April to June 2026, ranking 2nd of 16 suppliers.

products.name: Utility Warehouse
products.description: A telecoms and insurance bundler that also sells energy. Its own fuel mix disclosure for April 2025 to March 2026 shows 11 per cent renewable across the electricity it supplied.

price.note: Utility Warehouse's electricity tariff is bound by the same Ofgem price cap as other suppliers without a derogation.

environment.note: Utility Warehouse's own fuel mix disclosure for the electricity it supplied between 1 April 2025 and 31 March 2026 shows 65 per cent gas, 11 per cent coal, 11 per cent renewable, 7 per cent nuclear and 5 per cent other, with figures rounded and so not summing to 100 per cent.

transparency.note: Utility Warehouse's fuel mix page states its percentages plainly for 1 April 2025 to 31 March 2026 and notes that they are rounded, but does not mention REGO certificates or how any renewable share is backed.

accessibility.note: Citizens Advice gave Utility Warehouse an overall star rating of 2.63 out of 5 for April to June 2026, ranking 13th of 16 suppliers.

products.name: Utilita
products.description: A supplier built around prepayment meters and smart pay-as-you-go billing. It says publicly that no supplier can honestly claim a 100 per cent renewable tariff, a position its own fuel mix disclosure supports.

price.note: Utilita's electricity tariffs sit under the same Ofgem price cap as other suppliers without a derogation.

environment.note: Citizens Advice's April to June 2026 supplier page records Utilita's fuel mix as 83 per cent fossil fuel, 11 per cent nuclear, 0 per cent renewable and 7 per cent other. The page does not state the period the fuel mix covers.

transparency.note: Utilita's own sustainability page says 'No matter what suppliers say, there’s no such thing as a 100% renewable tariff. Every household receives the same electricity from the National Grid,' and offers a live grid mix so customers can see how their electricity is generated.

accessibility.note: Citizens Advice gave Utilita an overall star rating of 2.53 out of 5 for April to June 2026, ranking 15th of 16 suppliers, with 95.7 complaints per 10,000 customers.

products.name: So Energy
products.description: An independent supplier whose disclosed fuel mix is well above the national average for renewables. Its own page explaining how that share is sourced could not be read directly for this entry, so only the disclosed figures are scored here.

price.note: So Energy's electricity tariffs are bound by the same Ofgem price cap as other suppliers without a derogation.

environment.note: Citizens Advice's April to June 2026 supplier page records So Energy's fuel mix as 67 per cent renewable, 27 per cent fossil fuel, 4 per cent nuclear and 2 per cent other. The page does not state the period the fuel mix covers.

accessibility.note: Citizens Advice gave So Energy an overall star rating of 2.85 out of 5 for April to June 2026, ranking 11th of 16 suppliers.

products.name: Outfox Energy
products.description: A Leicester-based budget supplier, formerly Outfox the Market, that Ofgem fined 1.8 million pounds in 2023 for repeatedly failing to submit financial data the regulator had requested. Its customer service now ranks near the top of Citizens Advice's table.

price.note: Outfox Energy's tariffs are bound by the same Ofgem price cap as other suppliers without a derogation.

environment.note: Citizens Advice's April to June 2026 supplier page records Outfox Energy's fuel mix as 41 per cent renewable, 43 per cent fossil fuel, 14 per cent nuclear and 3 per cent other. The page does not state the period the fuel mix covers.

accessibility.note: Citizens Advice gave Outfox Energy an overall star rating of 4.03 out of 5 for April to June 2026, ranking 1st of 16 suppliers.

products.name: TruEnergy
products.description: A small supplier that Ofgem issued with a provisional order in July 2022 requiring an independent audit of how it sets customers' direct debits; Ofgem later decided not to confirm the order and it lapsed in October 2022. It ranks last on Citizens Advice's supplier table and discloses one of the lowest renewable shares in this list.

price.note: TruEnergy's tariffs are bound by the same Ofgem price cap as other suppliers without a derogation.

environment.note: Citizens Advice's April to June 2026 supplier page records TruEnergy's fuel mix as 8 per cent renewable, 76 per cent fossil fuel, 10 per cent nuclear and 6 per cent other. The page does not state the period the fuel mix covers.

accessibility.note: Citizens Advice gave TruEnergy an overall star rating of 1.38 out of 5 for April to June 2026, ranking last of 16 suppliers.

products.name: Co-op Energy
products.description: Owned by the Midcounties Co-operative and run on Octopus Energy's supply licence and technology. It funds a joint venture, Younity, that has backed more than 250 community energy projects, and puts 10 pounds from every new customer into a community energy fund.

price.note: EnergyCoop says it is 'a White label of Octopus Energy' and offers 'the same fixed and flexible tariffs as Octopus,' so it is scored with Octopus's capped tariffs. The page does not mention the Ofgem price cap.

environment.note: EnergyCoop, the brand behind Co-op Energy, says 'We only provide 100% renewable electricity' and describes its Community Power tariff as 'The UK's only tariff powered with 100% community-owned electricity.'

transparency.note: EnergyCoop says its Younity joint venture with Octopus has supported over 250 Community Energy projects and that for every new customer it puts 10 pounds into the Powering Communities Fund.

accessibility.note: Citizens Advice gave EnergyCoop, the brand behind Co-op Energy, an overall star rating of 3.64 out of 5 for April to June 2026, ranking 7th of 16 suppliers.
